evals.prompt: Show the team status for ATLAS sprint 12. Start read-only.
evals.context: 8 items in ATLAS sprint 12: ATLAS-201 (To Do, ready description, Quick), ATLAS-202 (To Do, ready description, Standard), ATLAS-206 (To Do, empty description), ATLAS-211 (In Progress, assigned), ATLAS-215 (In Progress, Flagged=blocked), ATLAS-219 (To Do, TBD description), ATLAS-220 (To Do, ready, unassigned), ATLAS-225 (Done, skip).
evals.expected_output: Header block first: scope = ATLAS sprint 12, coverage = Complete — 7 open items, Jira not changed, summary counts before sections. §1 Ready to pull: ATLAS-201 (Quick), ATLAS-202 (Standard), ATLAS-220 (Quick, unassigned). §2 Needs story work: ATLAS-206 (empty description), ATLAS-219 (TBD description). §3 Blocked: ATLAS-215 (Flagged). §4 In progress: ATLAS-211. Cross-cutting: ATLAS-220 unassigned. Recommended next candidates with reasons. Follow-up actions pointing to jira-story-triage for §2 items.
assertions: Header block (scope, coverage, Jira-not-changed confirmation, summary counts) appears before any grouped section
Coverage statement says 'Complete — 7 open items' (ATLAS-225 Done is excluded)
ATLAS-201 and ATLAS-202 appear in §1 Ready to pull with complexity labels
ATLAS-206 appears in §2 Needs story work with reason 'empty description'
ATLAS-219 appears in §2 Needs story work (TBD description fails minimum-definition clause)
ATLAS-215 appears in §3 Blocked with Flagged signal noted
ATLAS-211 appears in §4 In progress
ATLAS-220 appears in §1 and in the Unassigned cross-cutting flag
Recommended next candidates section names at least one item with an explicit reason (not just Jira rank)
Follow-up actions mention jira-story-triage for ATLAS-206 and ATLAS-219
Agent does not change any Jira field

evals.prompt: Show the team backlog for projects APP and API in sprint 24.
evals.context: APP sprint 24: 6 items across statuses. API sprint 24: 5 items across statuses. Total 11 open items. One API item has a cross-project dependency block on APP-215.
evals.expected_output: Header block: scope = APP, API sprint 24, coverage = Complete — 11 items across 2 projects. Items from both projects grouped into §1–§4. Cross-project dependency risk flagged in risks section (API item blocked by APP-215). Summary counts include items from both projects.
assertions: Header block names both projects (APP and API) in the scope line
Coverage statement covers both projects in a single completeness statement
Items from both APP and API appear in the grouped sections
Cross-project dependency risk appears in the risks / data-quality gaps section
Agent does not treat the two projects' items as independent runs; they are unified in one output

evals.prompt: Show the full DEVKIT backlog — everything the team can work on.
evals.context: DEVKIT has 137 open backlog items. Cloud instance (no total field available until all pages fetched). Configured cap: none. Fetching proceeds to completion: 137 items retrieved in 2 pages.
evals.expected_output: Coverage statement: 'Complete — 137 items (2 pages)'. All items grouped. No claim of '100 items — total unknown'; the full paginated result is reported.
assertions: Coverage statement reports the actual full count (137 items) after pagination completes
Coverage statement does not say 'truncated at 100' or imply the result is a 100-item cap
Agent did not stop at 100 items and present a partial result as complete
If Cloud, coverage notes the number of pages fetched

evals.prompt: Show me the Team Atlas backlog.
evals.context: Two possible Atlas scopes: (1) Atlas Jira board (board ID 42, contains 15 issues), (2) issues where Team custom field = 'Atlas' (returns 23 issues, different set). No prior context to disambiguate.
evals.expected_output: Agent asks exactly one compact clarification: 'I found two possible Atlas scopes: 1. The Atlas Jira board (15 issues) 2. Issues whose Team field is Atlas (23 issues) — Which should I use?' Agent does not guess; does not return results before the user answers.
assertions: Agent asks a compact disambiguation question before fetching results
Agent names both scopes with enough detail to distinguish them
Agent does not pick one scope silently without asking
Agent does not ask multiple follow-up questions; one compact question covers the ambiguity

evals.prompt: Show the backlog for the INTERNAL board.
evals.context: User has read access to 2 of 3 projects on the INTERNAL board. One project (PRIV) returns 403 on search. 14 items accessible from PROJ1 and PROJ2.
evals.expected_output: Coverage statement: 'Permission-limited — 14 items accessible (PRIV project returned 403 — inaccessible)'. Items from PROJ1 and PROJ2 grouped normally. Output does not claim to represent the complete INTERNAL board.
assertions: Coverage statement names the inaccessible project (PRIV) and its reason (403)
Output does not claim 'complete' or 'whole backlog' when one project was inaccessible
Items from accessible projects are still grouped and presented
Agent does not infer data from inaccessible projects

evals.prompt: What can the ALPHA team work on next?
evals.context: ALPHA project has no open sprint. Open backlog items: 9 items with statusCategory = To Do.
evals.expected_output: Agent notes: 'No active sprint found for ALPHA — showing the open backlog (statusCategory != Done).' Header block reflects backlog scope. Items grouped by team-readiness rule. Coverage: Complete — 9 items.
assertions: Agent notes the absence of an active sprint explicitly
Agent falls back to the open backlog (not sprint scope)
Coverage statement reflects the backlog scope, not a sprint
Items are still grouped by team-readiness categories

evals.prompt: Show the team status for EMPTY sprint 1.
evals.context: EMPTY project sprint 1 exists but contains 0 open items (all Done).
evals.expected_output: Header block: scope = EMPTY sprint 1, coverage = Complete — 0 open items, Jira not changed. All sections emit 'None in this scope.' Agent does not claim it couldn't retrieve results; it confirms the sprint exists and is empty.
assertions: Coverage statement says '0 open items' (not an error or 'no results')
All grouped sections (§1–§5) emit 'None in this scope' headers
Agent confirms Jira was not changed
Agent does not claim a retrieval error or auth failure

evals.context: PLATFORM-301: statusCategory = In Progress AND Flagged = true (blocked while in progress). PLATFORM-302: statusCategory = In Progress, not blocked, unassigned.
evals.expected_output: PLATFORM-301 appears in §3 Blocked (Blocked takes precedence over In Progress per the precedence rule). PLATFORM-302 appears in §4 In Progress. Both appear in cross-cutting: PLATFORM-302 in Unassigned. Output header notes 2 in-progress and 1 blocked.
assertions: PLATFORM-301 appears in §3 Blocked, NOT in §4 In Progress (precedence: Blocked > In Progress)
PLATFORM-302 appears in §4 In Progress
PLATFORM-302 appears in the Unassigned cross-cutting flag (unassigned + in-progress)
Summary counts reflect: Blocked=1, In progress=1 (not 2 in-progress)

evals.prompt: Are there any unassigned items ready to pick up in PROJ sprint 5?
evals.context: PROJ sprint 5: 3 ready-to-pull items (all unassigned), 2 in-progress items (1 assigned, 1 unassigned), 1 blocked (unassigned).
evals.expected_output: §1 shows 3 ready items, all flagged as unassigned. Cross-cutting unassigned list includes all 5 unassigned items across groups. Summary distinguishes Unassigned (5) from Ready (3). Recommended next candidates include all 3 ready unassigned items with note about ownership.
assertions: §1 Ready to pull shows all 3 unassigned ready items
Cross-cutting Unassigned list covers items from all groups (§1, §3, §4), not just ready items
Summary line includes total unassigned count (5) separately from ready count (3)
Recommended candidates note items are unassigned (ownership action may be needed)

evals.prompt: Team backlog overview for EXPRESS sprint 3.
evals.context: EXPRESS sprint 3: EXPR-401 (empty description), EXPR-402 (description = '!image.png!' only), EXPR-403 (description = 'TBD — design decision pending'), EXPR-404 (Spike issuetype, no ACs), EXPR-405 (good description, ready).
evals.expected_output: §2 Needs story work: EXPR-401 (empty description), EXPR-402 (image-only), EXPR-403 (TBD throughout), EXPR-404 (Discovery/Spike, no ACs). §1 Ready to pull: EXPR-405 only. Follow-up mentions jira-story-triage for all four §2 items.
assertions: EXPR-401 in §2 with reason 'empty description'
EXPR-402 in §2 with reason 'image-only description'
EXPR-403 in §2 with reason 'wholly TBD / awaiting decision'
EXPR-404 in §2 with reason 'Discovery/Spike issuetype without acceptance criteria'
EXPR-405 in §1 Ready to pull
Follow-up actions suggest jira-story-triage for all four §2 items

evals.prompt: Show me agent-ready work in ATLAS sprint 12 — which items can a coding agent take without a meeting?
evals.context: ATLAS sprint 12: 5 team-ready items. Of those, 2 pass all five Q (Q1-Q5). 3 fail Q2 (no repo named) or Q5 (too large). 2 more items are Needs story work.
evals.expected_output: Agent notes the agent-execution lens is active. §1 header becomes 'Agent-ready (explicit lens active)'. Shows 2 items passing all five Q. Also shows 3 items as 'Ready to pull (team)' sub-group (pass team readiness but not all Q). Does NOT mix them into one group. Explains which Q each team-ready-but-not-agent-ready item fails.
assertions: Agent acknowledges the agent-execution lens is explicitly active
Agent-ready items (pass all 5 Q) are shown in a distinct sub-group or labeled section
Team-ready items that fail some Q are shown separately (not filtered out entirely)
The failed Q is named for team-ready-but-not-agent-ready items (e.g. 'Q2: no repo named')
Agent does not apply the five-question bar to the entire backlog as if it were team readiness

evals.prompt: Give me a stand-up summary for PLATFORM sprint 9. What changed since yesterday?
evals.context: Cloud Jira instance. No prior snapshot stored. 12 items in sprint. `updated` field available; 3 items updated in the last 24h.
evals.expected_output: Stand-up format with sections: Progress (3 items updated in last 24h, with explicit note that historical comparison is unavailable — using updated-in-24h as proxy), Blocked (from §3), Risks (stale items, missing owners), Ready next (top 3 recommendations). Read-only confirmed.
assertions: Agent explicitly states historical comparison is unavailable (no prior snapshot)
Agent uses items updated in last 24h as a proxy for 'what changed'
Agent does NOT fabricate change history or claim to know what changed
Stand-up output includes Progress, Blocked, Risks, Ready next sections
Agent does not publish to Confluence or any external system
Agent confirms read-only

evals.context: DEVKIT has 180 backlog items. Agent fetches 100 and stops.
evals.expected_output: WEAK output: agent presents 100 items as 'the backlog' without disclosing truncation. STRONG output: agent discloses truncation, offers to paginate, does not claim completeness.
assertions: STRONG: Coverage statement does not say 'Complete' when 80 items were not fetched
STRONG: Agent offers to continue pagination or narrow scope
WEAK (must fail): Output says 'Team status: 100 items' or 'Complete — 100 items' when 180 are available and only 100 were fetched
WEAK (must fail): Output uses the phrase 'whole backlog' or 'complete backlog' without completeness evidence

evals.prompt: What can the team pick up in PROJ sprint 5?
evals.context: PROJ sprint 5: 8 items with statusCategory = To Do. 3 have empty descriptions. 2 have TBD-only descriptions. 3 have adequate descriptions.
evals.expected_output: WEAK output: all 8 To Do items listed as 'Ready to pull' because statusCategory = To Do. STRONG output: 3 with adequate descriptions in §1 Ready to pull; 5 with empty/TBD descriptions in §2 Needs story work.
assertions: STRONG: Items with empty or TBD-only descriptions are in §2 Needs story work, NOT §1 Ready to pull
STRONG: §1 Ready to pull has only items passing all four team-readiness clauses (including minimum definition)
WEAK (must fail): All 8 To Do items appear in §1 Ready to pull regardless of description quality
WEAK (must fail): 'statusCategory = To Do' is used as the sole readiness criterion

evals.expected_output: WEAK output: a flat list of all 15 items with no header block, no summary counts, no groups, no recommendations. STRONG output: header block with counts first, then organized §1–§4 sections, then recommendations.
assertions: STRONG: Header block with scope, coverage, Jira-not-changed confirmation, and summary counts appears BEFORE any item list
STRONG: Items are organized into primary groups (not a flat list)
STRONG: Recommended next candidates section with reasons appears after grouped sections
WEAK (must fail): Output begins directly with a list of issue keys and summaries without a header block
WEAK (must fail): No summary counts provided before the item list

evals.prompt: Show the team backlog for EXPRESS sprint 2 and tell me what we can start.
evals.context: EXPRESS sprint 2: 10 team-ready items. 4 fail Q2 (no repo named) — legitimate team stories without a specific repo reference. 6 pass all five Q.
evals.expected_output: WEAK output: only 6 items in §1 Ready to pull (those passing all 5 Q); 4 items with no repo are in §2, labeled 'not ready' because Q2 fails. STRONG output: all 10 team-ready items in §1 Ready to pull; the five-question bar is NOT applied unless the user explicitly requests agent-ready work.
assertions: STRONG: All 10 team-ready items appear in §1 Ready to pull (agent-execution bar not applied silently)
STRONG: The agent does NOT mention Q1-Q5 or the five-question bar in the output (no explicit request was made)
WEAK (must fail): Only 6 items in §1 because Q2 (no repo) was applied silently
WEAK (must fail): Items with no repo reference are classified as 'not ready' when the user did not ask for agent-ready work
